lessonRef.subject: ready-for-life
lessonRef.title: Independent application: making a request or an enquiry of an office

objective: Learners draft a professional inquiry message to a real local public office about a genuine question they have, using the workplace-message conventions from an earlier unit, without sending it.
scenario: The learner identifies one real local public office or service (such as a library, transit authority, or health department) and one genuine question they'd actually want answered, then drafts a short, specific inquiry message using the subject-greeting-body-closing structure, kept as a draft only.
safetyNotes: This message is drafted for practice only and is never sent as part of this lesson.
materials: the subject-greeting-body-closing structure from an earlier unit

tasks.directions: Name one real local public office and one genuine question you'd want answered.

prompts.text: Name the office and the specific question, and explain why it's a genuine question for you, not a made-up one.

tasks.directions: Draft your inquiry message using the four-part structure: subject line, greeting, body, closing.

prompts.text: My subject line names the specific topic of my question.
My body states exactly one clear question.
My closing includes my name and enough context for the office to respond usefully.

tasks.directions: Read your draft as if you were a busy staff member receiving it, and revise anything unclear.

prompts.text: Name one thing you revised to make the question easier for a busy staff member to answer quickly.

tasks.directions: Reflect on inquiring of a public office versus a private business.

prompts.text: Name one way you'd expect a public office's response process to differ from a private business responding to a customer.

remediation: If a learner's question is vague or bundles multiple questions into one message, reteach by requiring the body to contain exactly one question stated in a single clear sentence, splitting any multi-part question into the single most important one for this draft.
extension: Have the learner draft a second inquiry to a different type of public office and compare which one required more background context to make the question answerable.
